title: Hiding among the baggage (1 Samuel 10:17–24)
hookLine: chosen as king, tall Saul hides among the luggage
tomorrow: The Lord looks on the heart

cards: The whole nation is gathered at Mizpeh to find out who their king will be, and they're choosing by lot. Tribe by tribe, the lot narrows. The tribe of Benjamin is taken.
Then one family in Benjamin. Then one man: Saul, the son of Kish. Every head turns.
And the text says, "when they sought him, he could not be found." The king is missing from his own coronation. So they enquire of the LORD further: where is he?
And the answer comes back, in the King James words: "Behold, he hath hid himself among the stuff."

teach.h: THE STUFF: THE GEAR AND THE BAGS.
teach.b: The stuff is the baggage: the gear and supplies people brought to the gathering. Somewhere behind the packs, the new king is crouching. And he's not easy to hide.
When they fetch him and he stands up, "he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward." Taller than everyone, folded up behind the luggage. Why hide?
The story has given clues. In the chapter before, Saul was out looking for his father's lost donkeys when he met Samuel.
Samuel told him the desire of all Israel was on him, and Saul answered, "Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel?" Then Samuel anointed him in private with a vial of oil.
So when the lot falls, Saul has already been anointed, and he hides anyway. Fear, modesty, dread of the weight: the text doesn't say which, and readers have heard all three.
Samuel presents him: "See ye him whom the LORD hath chosen, that there is none like him among all the people?"
And the people shout, "God save the king." One more detail, just past today's verses. Not everyone cheers.
Some say, how shall this man save us, and they despise him and bring him no gifts.
"But he held his peace." Some readers who know how Saul's story ends come back to this chapter, to the tall, frightened man behind the bags, before anything went wrong.

how: Christians read Saul's hiding as a very human moment at the start of a story that ends in tragedy, and preachers sometimes use it to talk about the fear that comes with being called.

games.q: you're Saul. you were anointed in secret. now the whole nation is drawing lots, and it's narrowing to your family. what do you do?
o: step forward before your name is called.
slip away and hide among the baggage.
stand still and wait for the lot.
games.why: when they sought him, he could not be found. the LORD told them: he hath hid himself among the stuff (10:21–22).

practice: Ask where you're hiding among the stuff right now: a role you keep dodging, a conversation that's yours to have, a gift tucked behind busyness or being too tired.
Let one come to mind, and without stepping out yet, picture standing up from behind the bags, all the way up. If you pray, ask for courage to be found.
